title: Parser fixtures invented from assumption pass unit tests but produce 0 entries on the real file — verify against the actual data file before shipping
trigger: A text/binary parser is implemented against an assumed format and its unit tests use fixtures written from the same assumption
principle: Unit tests written from the same wrong assumption as the parser prove nothing. Before shipping a parser, run it once on the real production file and check the output count/content. Structural anchors come from the real file's spec, not from what the fixture looks like. Also: a 'ready' status derived only from 'process ran' (timestamp set, file picked) is a false positive — surface the result count so an empty parse can't masquerade as success.

cases.context: Lingvo DSL audio index: parser assumed headwords wrapped in `[word]...[/word]` tags (invented format). Real ForvoEnglish.dsl uses standard Lingvo layout — bare headword lines at column 0 + tab-indented card body containing `[s]path[/s]` tags. Build index reported 'Indexed 0 entries' while the UI status dot still showed green 'ready' because readiness only checked file-picked + lastIndexedAt.

applyFor: Any parser written for an external file format (DSL, SRT, VTT, dictionary, archive)
Index/extraction pipelines where 'process ran' is reported separately from 'results produced'
Status/readiness indicators that can go green on empty output
